one_liner: Small MIT C++ BT.709 RGB/YUV 4:2:0 converter (SSE2/SSSE3/AVX2/NEON) whose README claims to beat libyuv and Accelerate.
what_it_does: Converts 8-bit RGB24/RGBA (optionally BGR/BGRA via a swizzle flag) to and from YU12 (I420), YV12, NV12 and NV21 with BT.709 full- or video-range coefficients, plus a YUV-to-packed-YUVA helper and an experimental Apple AMX decoder for YU12. The API is a C-style parameter struct per format (yuv2rgb_yu12(&p), rgb2yuv_nv12(&p)) with optional per-plane pointers and strides, plus inline convenience overloads that take one contiguous YUV buffer. It is not a drop-in for libyuv's function names or matrix choices.
how_it_is_fast: Each converter is one template instantiated per (channels, swizzle, interleaved, U-first, range) combination and compiled several times from the same .inl file with HAVE_NEON/SSE2/SSSE3/AVX2 defined, then picked once by CPUID into a function-local static pointer. Kernels process two rows at a time with 8-bit fixed-point coefficients: decode uses 16-bit mulhi (x86) or 8-bit widening multiplies (NEON_FAST, always on for ARM), encode uses maddubs+hadd (SSSE3/AVX2) or widening multiply-accumulate with pairwise adds for 2x2 chroma averaging (NEON), and results are interleaved with unpack transposes or vld4/vst4. Precision is traded for fewer, narrower multiplies.
when_to_use: Converting RGBA/BGRA frames to or from I420/NV12/NV21 with BT.709 coefficients when the width is a multiple of 32 (AVX2) or 16 (SSE2/NEON).
Apple Silicon or AVX2 desktops where you want a few-file MIT source drop instead of building libyuv.
Preview, thumbnail or GPU-upload paths where a 1-3 code-value difference from a reference converter is acceptable.
Projects built with Clang or MSVC, where the per-function target attributes (Clang) or MSVC's intrinsic rules let the runtime dispatch work as written.
when_not_to_use: RGB24 (3-channel) data: every SIMD loop runs only for 4 channels, so 3-channel conversion is the scalar loop on all CPUs, and the scalar encoder applies the R coefficient to byte 2 (the SIMD encoders and the decoder treat byte 0 as R), so RGB24 encode swaps R and B unless the swizzle flag is inverted.

Widths that are not a multiple of the SIMD block: for 4-channel and YUVA conversions the code skips the scalar tail ('if (componentRGB == 4) continue;' after the SIMD loop), leaving the rightmost (halfWidth mod 8, or mod 16 on AVX2) x2 columns unwritten, e.g. 24 columns of a 1080-wide frame on AVX2.

Video-range content with super-whites on ARM: the NEON decode narrows (Y-16)*149>>7 with a non-saturating vshrn_n_u16, so luma 236-255 wraps to 0-22 (near black); the x86 paths keep 16 bits and do not wrap.
Anything beyond 8-bit 4:2:0 BT.709: no BT.601 or BT.2020, no 4:2:2/4:4:4, no 10-bit, no scaling or rotation.
Code that needs maintenance or tests: last commit 20 Oct 2021, no tests in the repository, and the linked benchmark harness cannot be found.

integration.dependencies: none (Apple Accelerate is only a benchmark comparison; the AMX path uses undocumented Apple instructions taken from dougallj's reverse-engineering gists)
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 for the designated-initializer convenience wrappers in yuv2rgb.h, rgb2yuv.h and yuv.h (define xxYUV_DEPRECATED to drop them); Clang or MSVC for working runtime dispatch; no build files are provided
integration.platforms: x86/x86-64 (SSE2 baseline, SSSE3 and AVX2 chosen at run time by CPUID), 32/64-bit ARM with NEON, Apple M1 AMX for YU12 decode; other targets get the scalar loop. AVX-512 kernels exist in yuv2rgb.inl but are never instantiated.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; the converters keep no shared mutable state and pick the kernel through C++11 function-local statics, so concurrent calls look safe (inference from the code).

gotchas: The planar entry points pass strideU twice (converter(..., strideY, strideU, strideU, ...)), so a caller-supplied strideV is ignored in yuv2rgb_yu12/yv12 and rgb2yuv_yu12/yv12.

Under GCC the target-attribute macro expands to nothing (it is defined only for __llvm__), so the AVX2/SSSE3 kernels need -mavx2/-mssse3 on the whole file, which also lets the compiler use AVX2 in the fallback paths and defeats the CPUID dispatch (inference from the macro).

Outputs differ by platform: NEON_FAST uses 6-7 bit chroma coefficients (full-range B gain 1.844 vs 1.863), x86 decode scales by coefficient*255/256, and the SSSE3/AVX2 encoders halve the luma weights so full-range white encodes to Y=253 (254 on NEON and scalar, both truncating).
Odd widths or heights lose the last column or row (loops run over width>>1 and height>>1).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick xxYUV over libyuv, sparkyuv or yuvutils-rs only when you need a tiny MIT C++ drop for BT.709 RGBA/NV12 on M1 or AVX2 with 32-pixel-aligned widths; sparkyuv covers 4:4:4 to 4:1:0, NV16/NV24 and many matrices, yuvutils-rs is the Rust option with like-for-like rows against libyuv, and libyuv stays the safe default for odd sizes, RGB24 and other matrices.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README tables give microseconds per conversion for xxYUV against libyuv (version and matrix not stated) and Apple Accelerate on an Apple M1 (NEON, plus x86 rows presumably under Rosetta) and an i7-8700B (AVX2): about 1.2-1.55x faster encode and 1.3x (AVX2) to 3.2x (M1 NEON) faster decode than libyuv. Compiler, flags, image size and pixel layout are not stated and the harness is not public; because only the 4-channel paths are vectorised, the SIMD rows must be RGBA/BGRA, and the microsecond scale implies a small cache-resident image (inference).
status_note: Abandoned since October 2021 (64 commits, 2 closed questions, no PRs, no tests) but MIT-licensed and about fifteen small files, so it is easy to vendor if you first fix the tail, strideV, video-range wrap and RGB24 channel-order bugs.
